column3: The thorp's record of crimes at Ögedeikul is neither short nor growing: the law and the criminals are close to even, and the next few seasons will decide which way it goes.
This is how Ögedeikul looks on a first visit; a season there might show it differently.
The country around Ögedeikul is thick with creatures and the thorp has answered it properly: there is a wall to hold and there are people to hold it, and both are in use constantly.
The walls and townsfolk of Ögedeikul would see off a raid but not a proper army, and nothing now under way will change that.
The thorp settles things itself, quickly, and does not always settle them well.
Ögedeikul has been short of money for years, and each lean season leaves less to spend when a real crisis comes.
Ögedeikul could keep soldiers and does not; the thorp has decided that arming itself when needed costs less than paying anybody to be armed all year.
Ögedeikul retains no specialists. Whatever comes out of the country is met by whoever the thorp has, whether or not they are the right answer to it.
Nothing unseen is known to have come at Ögedeikul, but the thorp keeps no wards or seers that would notice if it had.
Ögedeikul has not been attacked lately, and if it were, it would struggle to hold.
Ögedeikul's defences are sound, but fewer people turn out each season to man the palisade, and the thorp is slow to notice.
What goes wrong at Ögedeikul goes wrong one thing at a time and belongs to whoever did it.
Whatever is run at Ögedeikul is run outside the hall, and business with the hall is straight.
